verdicts.strongest_argument: Every input to this arithmetic is published and at least one retail-facing outlet has already run the same subtraction. The 20-F (2026-03-30) discloses cash of $111,112,251, a $87.1m working capital deficit, $102.1m of SHORT-TERM borrowings, $50.1m long-term, and -- far harsher than anything the claim concludes -- an explicit 'substantial doubt about our ability to continue as a going concern.' The January raise (62.5m shares at $4.00, closed 2026-01-21) and the $230m all-cash Reward payment (2026-02-10) were both wire events. merlintrader's RZLV hub already states the net position is 'broadly in the same region as where it started' and that no repurchase had been announced as of 2026-08-04. A market that has been told 'going concern doubt' does not need to be told 'the $300m buyback is only single-digit-percent fundable' -- the stronger fact is out and the stock is 63% below its 52w high. Separately, the load-bearing premise is weaker than presented: 398,827,587 is the count stockanalysis carries, which is plausibly the 20-F cover-page figure struck after the January close, so it does NOT establish zero issuance February-August 2026 -- particularly with the going-concern paragraph naming an active ATM program as a mitigation. The genuinely new datum is the actual 30-Jun-2026 cash number, and that is one line of the print, not an unpriced insight.

verdicts.strongest_argument: I concede the publication test: I searched and found no market-facing coverage of the plc's Companies House delinquency, and I independently verified the register does show 'Accounts overdue' with last accounts made up to 31 December 2024 against a 30 June 2026 due date. The marginal RZLV holder is a US retail/momentum holder reading GlobeNewswire, not the UK register, so this is genuinely obscure. But it is obscure and small in the same breath: the company filed a 20-F on time on 2026-03-30 with audited FY2025 statements and furnished the Annual Report as a 6-K exhibit, so the information content of the UK statutory filing is nil -- this is a compliance-calendar failure, not a withheld number. There is also no mechanism into the 09-01 print: the 6-K will not mention Companies House and the interims are unaudited by construction. One sub-claim is wrong: resolutions filed at the register on 22 July 2026 almost certainly record the AGM held 30 June 2026 (the same meeting that carried the buyback mandate), so the auditor resolution was passed ON the statutory deadline, not 'three weeks after' it -- the hunter has read a filing date as a passing date.

verdicts.strongest_argument: Split the claim. The debt facts are fully published: the 20-F carries $102.1m as short-term borrowings and $50.1m long-term, and stocktitan headlined the filing 'Rezolve AI 20-F details losses and going-concern risk' on 2026-03-30. The mid-September court timetable for the capital reduction is in the company's own 2026-06-30 release. What is not published anywhere I can find is that the charges sit on the LISTED PARENT rather than a US subsidiary, and the inference that secured creditors get formal creditor protection in a s.641 court-sanctioned reduction -- that is a real, non-obvious channel by which the buyback could slip, and it is the part I score low. Two things cap the number. First, the mechanism resolves at a mid-September hearing, not at the 09-01 print, so it reaches this event only if management addresses it on the call. Second, the claim mis-assigns the lenders: it calls the $102m 'Crownpeak/Monroe term loans', whereas the 20-F and this brief's own RZLV-h2#2 put $101,540,086 with Monroe (short-term) and $50,000,000 with Crownpeak (promissory notes). Crownpeak Technology Holdings is the acquisition seller, and seller-note creditors routinely consent as part of a negotiated deal, which materially softens the creditor-veto story.

verdicts.strongest_argument: This is the finding whose own numbers refute its materiality. The $63,345,577 FY2025 impairment is a named line in the 20-F income statement and was summarised by stocktitan on 2026-03-30, and the 'continued volatility could force further impairments' warning is the company's own published risk factor -- so the existence of the risk is out. The magnitude is bounded and trivial: total digital assets on the 31-Dec-2025 balance sheet are only ~$16.4m ('other digital assets') plus ~$0.1m crypto intangibles, and Rezolve's stated policy is to add SQD equal to roughly 1% of revenue (~$1.3m a half). The claim's own price path -- $0.0627 in January to a $0.056-0.058 zone by June -- is a ~10-14% decline, i.e. roughly $2m of writedown against a $1.14bn market cap, or 0.2%. Even a total write-off of the whole $16.4m is 1.4% of cap and lands in a non-cash line inside a company that already printed a $101.4m net loss. The 'no consensus on the net loss line' observation is true but this name trades on the revenue/ARR narrative and five analysts carry a $10.50 target; nobody is marking it on the impairment line.

verdicts.strongest_argument: The strongest of the eight, and I only partly resist it. I verified the filing exists: Companies House shows group accounts for Reward Loyalty UK Limited (10701520) year ended 30 April 2025, filed 25 July 2026, 74 pages. I found no market-facing coverage of its contents, and the gross-margin (~40%) and ~GBP2m EBITDA detail is genuinely unpublished. Three things stop this being a 10. First, the order-of-magnitude gap was already checkable before the deal: aggregators carry ~GBP53m turnover for Reward's YE 30 April 2024 accounts, filed 31 January 2025 -- thirteen months before Rezolve told investors the asset added 'approximately $90 million of EBITDA-accretive revenue.' Anyone who pulled the register in February 2026 saw the same gap. Second, the frame has circulated: Fuzzy Panda's report of 2025-09-29 is explicitly 'Faking ARR by Acquiring Failing AI Start-ups w/ Declining Revenue', which is this exact allegation applied to this exact strategy, and the stock fell on it. Third, the number is disclosed by the event itself -- the 09-01 interims consolidate Reward from 10 February and will show the blended gross margin, so this is less 'unpriced fact' than 'correct prediction of a line item hours away'. Note the $90m may be a forward run-rate or a wider Reward group perimeter, which the hunter does not exclude.

verdicts.strongest_argument: The gross-margin collapse from 95.8% to 66.0% is not a discovery -- it is two published numbers, and I reproduced the second directly from the 20-F XBRL: revenue $46,800,099 less cost of revenue $15,922,202 equals $30,877,897, exactly 66.0%. That filing is five months old, and merlintrader's public RZLV hub already prints 'audited FY2025 gross margin was 66.0% on revenue of $46.8 million.' What is not written down anywhere is the implied ~61% H2 2025 exit rate, and the forward step-down from consolidating a ~40%-margin Reward on top of Crownpeak and GroupBy -- that is the live content, and it rests on the same Companies House PDF as RZLV-h2#0, so the two findings are one bet, not two. The counterweight is that this is a pure guess about a line item the print will disclose in a few hours; the market's problem with RZLV has never been gross margin, it has been whether the revenue is real. A company that can hold 60% while 20x-ing revenue would be read bullishly by the same holders who bid the stock 22% on a press release with no contract value.

verdicts.strongest_argument: The first half of this is priced by identity, not by argument: the run-up attribution is arithmetically exact -- 2.8375 divided by the 2.43 close of 08-24 is 1.1677, precisely the baseline's +16.77% five-day figure -- and the 08-25 release moved the stock roughly +22% intraday on the day it was published on GlobeNewswire and covered by Yahoo, Manila Times, Kalkine, martechseries and stocktitan. A price move caused by a document everyone read is the definition of in the price. The 'no contract value, no term, no Google quote' observation is visible on the face of that same press release, and the paid-partnership frame was published by Fuzzy Panda on 2025-09-29 ('partnerships with Microsoft and Google are not true collaborations but arrangements where Rezolve pays the tech giants'), so the skepticism has already circulated and been traded. And the claim's central piece of corroborating evidence is self-defeating: Rezolve ACQUIRED Subsquid on 2025-10-09, so Google Cloud Web3 documentation naming Subsquid for exactly this indexing function is confirmation that Rezolve's technology is in the stack, not evidence against it. That is the one factual error in this brief that I would call load-bearing.

verdicts.strongest_argument: The headline arithmetic is a subtraction anyone can do and somebody already has: $360m minus $127m is $233m, and merlintrader's public hub states 'roughly $233 million in second-half revenue -- approximately 1.8 times the preliminary first-half figure of $127 million.' Both inputs were wire copy (2026-07-27 preliminary H1, guidance reaffirmed 2026-07-27 and again 2026-08-06 alongside the 09-01 call notice). The additive content is the acquired-run-rate decomposition, and it rests on the same Reward Loyalty PDF as RZLV-h2#0 -- same document, same bet. It also has a soft spot: Reward consolidated only from 10 February, so H1 carried roughly 4.7 of 6 months of it, which means the acquired base in H1 is nearer $75m than $84m and the residual is nearer $50m than $43m; and H2 mechanically picks up the missing Reward stub plus a full half of anything closed mid-year, which is part of how the company gets to a $500m exit ARR claim. The bear case here is 'the guide is a stretch', which is exactly what a stock 63% below its 52-week high on 86% realised vol with a Fuzzy Panda report on file already says.

adversary_notes: Three substantive points on the name. (1) The brief is eight-for-eight bearish. There is not one bullish finding to attack, which is itself a caution: the option tape gives no directional statement at all (no 25-delta skew recoverable, put/call open interest 0.25 -- call-heavy, not put-bid), the ATM spread is 40% of mid so the 12.04% event implied move is nearly meaningless, and n=0 prior reactions means there is no reaction history to lean on. A one-sided brief on a name where the market has not expressed a direction should not be read as eight independent shorts. (2) One claim I believe is factually wrong in a way that matters: RZLV-h2#3 argues the Google release is hollow because Google's Web3 documentation names Subsquid and Chainstack rather than Rezolve. Rezolve acquired Subsquid on 2025-10-09 (https://www.globenewswire.com/news-release/2025/10/09/3164101). Google naming Subsquid is therefore consistent with the release, and the same SQD holdings are the subject of RZLV-h1#3 -- the hunter has used Subsquid as evidence against Rezolve in one finding and as Rezolve's own impaired asset in another. (3) One claim is wrong on a date: RZLV-h1#1 treats the 22 July 2026 filing of the auditor resolution as the date it was passed 'three weeks after the statutory deadline'; the AGM that carried the buyback mandate was 30 June 2026, so the resolution was passed on the deadline and merely filed later. Also worth flagging: the load-bearing premise of RZLV-h1#0 -- 398,827,587 shares proving zero issuance since January -- may simply be the 20-F cover-page count struck after the January close, and the 20-F's own going-concern mitigation names an active ATM. Two of the CH facts I did verify myself and could not find published anywhere: the plc's 'Accounts overdue' flag, and the existence of Reward's 74-page YE-30-Apr-2025 group accounts filed 2026-07-25.
interactions: Three clusters share documents. (a) RZLV-h1#0 and RZLV-h2#2 are the same cash-bound bet from the same 20-F, differing only in decimal places -- they should not be counted twice, and RZLV-h2#2 is the better-sourced version. (b) RZLV-h1#2 and RZLV-h2#2 both rest on the Companies House charges page and CONTRADICT each other on the facts: h1#2 calls the ~$102m 'Crownpeak/Monroe term loans maturing 31 Dec 2026', while h2#2 correctly separates $101,540,086 Monroe (short-term per the 20-F) from $50,000,000 Crownpeak notes. (c) RZLV-h2#0, RZLV-h2#1 and RZLV-h2#4 all rest on the single Reward Loyalty UK Limited YE-30-Apr-2025 group accounts PDF filed 2026-07-25, which the hunter concedes was read only through aggregators. If that GBP52.89m turnover or the ~40% gross margin is wrong or covers a different perimeter than Rezolve bought, all three fail together. Finally, RZLV-h1#3 and RZLV-h2#3 point in opposite directions on Subsquid: h1#3 needs the SQD holding to be a real, impairable balance-sheet asset, while h2#3 uses Subsquid's presence in Google's documentation as evidence Rezolve is not there.
